key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of his forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove with localized linear hair loss, combined with histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and positive direct immunofluorescence, is most consistent with Discoid Lupus Erythematosus.

rejected.label: Lichen Planopilaris
rejected.why: While lichen planopilaris can cause scarring alopecia, the patient's lack of symptoms such as pruritus and the specific histopathologic findings are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia
rejected.why: Frontal fibrosing alopecia typically presents with band-like hair loss and is more common in postmenopausal women, which does not match the patient's profile.

rejected.label: Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia
rejected.why: This condition typically starts at the vertex and progresses centrifugally, which does not match the patient's linear, arc-shaped lesion.

rejected.label: Alopecia Areata
rejected.why: Alopecia areata usually presents with well-defined, round patches of hair loss, which does not match the patient's linear, depressed skin groove.

rejected.label: Traction Alopecia
rejected.why: Traction alopecia is caused by mechanical stress on the hair follicles, which the patient denied any history of.
